legend: Have you ever been to a boring lesson with absolutely nothing to do? Everyone deals with it differently: some students prefer to train their art skills, some try to compensate for the lack of sleep, and Lucas is the only one in this class who does robotics instead.

Lucas has just programmed a robot. It draws a polyline on the 2D plane using a simple algorithm. Initially, the pencil controlled by the robot is located at the point $$$(0, 0)$$$ and faces right along the vector $$$(1, 0)$$$. Then, the following pair of actions is repeatedly performed:
the robot draws a segment of length $$$1$$$ and turns the direction clockwise by $$$\alpha$$$ degrees;
the robot draws a segment of length $$$1$$$ and turns the direction counterclockwise by $$$\beta$$$ degrees.

If the pencil returns to $$$(0, 0)$$$ for the first time, and the resulting polyline does not intersect itself, the robot stops, and Lucas calls it a successful operation. In that case, Lucas wonders what the area of the figure bounded by the drawn polyline is.

We say that the polyline intersects itself if two of its segments have a common point other than a shared vertex of adjacent segments. Segments are adjacent if they are consecutive while drawing, and the first and the last segments are also adjacent if the polyline has returned to $$$(0, 0)$$$ for the first time.
input: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \leq t \leq 10^4$$$): the number of test cases. Then, $$$t$$$ test cases follow.
The only line of a test case contains two integers $$$\alpha$$$ and $$$\beta$$$ ($$$1 \leq \alpha, \beta \leq 179$$$).
output: For each test case, print the area of the figure on a separate line if the robot succeeds, or $$$-1$$$ otherwise. If the printed value is not $$$-1$$$, the absolute or relative error must not exceed $$$10^{-6}$$$.
note: The figures below correspond to the example test cases (with possibly different scales of figures).
In the third test case of the example, the polyline intersects itself, and the figure is drawn only up to the first intersection.

legend.ai: 你是否曾经上过无聊透顶、完全无事可做的课？每个人应对的方式都不一样：有些学生喜欢练习艺术技能，有些则试图补觉，而 Lucas 是班上唯一选择做机器人项目的人。
Lucas 刚刚编写了一个机器人程序。机器人会使用一个简单的算法在二维平面上绘制一条折线。初始时，机器人控制的铅笔位于点 $$$(0, 0)$$$，并沿着向量 $$$(1, 0)$$$ 朝右。随后，机器人会不断重复执行以下一对操作：
机器人画出一条长度为 $$$1$$$ 的线段，并将方向顺时针旋转 $$$\alpha$$$ 度；
机器人画出一条长度为 $$$1$$$ 的线段，并将方向逆时针旋转 $$$\beta$$$ 度。
如果铅笔第一次回到 $$$(0, 0)$$$，且最终得到的折线不与自身相交，机器人就会停止，卢卡斯称之为一次成功的操作。此时，卢卡斯想知道由所画折线围成的图形面积是多少。
如果一条折线的两个线段有公共点，且该公共点不是相邻线段的公共端点，则称这条折线与自身相交。若两个线段在绘制过程中相邻，则称它们相邻；如果折线首次返回 $$$(0, 0)$$$，那么第一个线段和最后一个线段也相邻。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \leq t \leq 10^4$$$)，表示测试用例的数量。接下来有 $$$t$$$ 个测试用例。
测试用例仅一行，包含两个整数 $$$\alpha$$$ 和 $$$\beta$$$($$$1 \leq \alpha, \beta \leq 179$$$)。

output.ai: 对于每个测试用例，如果机器人成功，则单独输出该图形的面积；否则输出 $$$-1$$$。如果输出的值不是 $$$-1$$$，则绝对误差或相对误差不得超过 $$$10^{-6}$$$。

note.ai: 下图对应于示例测试用例（图形的比例可能不同）。
在示例的第三组测试数据中，折线与自身相交，图形只画到第一次相交的位置。
